<reason>Both sides built coherent cases, but A's central attack landed harder and went substantially unanswered: A repeatedly showed (A2.3, A2.4, A4.7-8, A5.5) that B's own product-vs-profile line explicitly permits B's flagship villain — the desperate midnight shopper facing few alternatives — because time-of-purchase and local competition are "transaction features" under B's own framework. B never directly rebutted this loophole in B's own proposed remedy, which is damaging because it means B's "disclose or ban" rule fails to fix the very harm B built its case around. A also opened with a genuinely reframing move (uniform pricing after disclosure levels prices up to the ceiling, not down to the floor), and while B's "algorithm exploits inattention not poverty" response weakened this somewhat, A sustained the frame into closing. B did land a strong late point (closing) that algorithmic personalization is specifically designed to defeat the "second tab"/marginal-shopper discipline A relies on, and A's closing answer to this was thin, mostly reasserting the discount-off-ceiling framing rather than engaging the mechanism. But A's unanswered loophole critique is more structurally damaging to B's affirmative burden (the proposed remedy itself), while A's own fallback case (scalpel bans on deception/protected traits) survives even if pure market discipline is imperfect. B was also somewhat evasive answering A's pointed pressure question (Q2, asking for an instance where exposure led to extending low prices rather than withdrawing them), pivoting to already-disclosed categories rather than confronting the asymmetry A named. On balance, A did more damage to B's core mechanism than B did to A's, giving A a clear but not overwhelming edge.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's repeated point that B's own product-vs-profile line permits pricing on "time of purchase and local competition" (A2.3/A4.7), meaning B's flagship villain (the desperate midnight shopper) is licensed rather than banned under B's proposed rule — a structural loophole in B's remedy that was never directly closed.</best_rebuttal>
